name: unxip
baseline: xip(1) and Archive Utility (Apple's Bom) for extracting Xcode .xip files
verdict_reason: The author claims about 2-3x less decompression time and about 25% less disk use than xip, with no published timings. xcodes, which ships unxip, independently says 'up to 70% faster on some systems', which points the same way but suggests a smaller and hardware-dependent gain.
tier_reason: First-party claim without timings, hardware or method; the second source is a downstream user with a vaguer figure.
claimed_speedup: About 2-3x less time decompressing and about 25% less disk space than Bom (xip, Archive Utility); up to 70% faster on some systems (xcodes)
install: Homebrew, MacPorts, release binary, or swiftc -O unxip.swift
one_liner: Swift tool that extracts Xcode .xip files about 2-3x faster than xip(1) and Archive Utility, per its author.
how_it_is_fast: unxip treats extraction as a pipeline of async streams (raw XIP data, decompressed chunks, files) built on Swift Concurrency, so decompression and disk writes overlap across cores. It writes the extracted files with compression, which is where the space saving comes from.
use_it_when: Installing Xcode versions on CI machines or developer Macs, where extraction takes minutes
Machines with many cores and fast APFS storage
skip_it_when: When the XIP's signature must be verified: unxip does no signature checking
Non-APFS or slow disks, where the author warns behavior is less tested
caveats: No timings, hardware or Xcode archive version are published for the 2-3x claim
'Up to 70% faster on some systems' (xcodes) is ambiguous and suggests the gain varies by machine
tradeoffs: Skips signature verification, so use a checksum or trusted download source
LGPL-3.0, which matters if you embed libunxip

evidence.quote: Its goal is to outperform Bom (which powers `xip(1)` and Archive Utility) in both performance and on-disk usage, and (at the time of writing) does so by a factor of about 2-3x in time spent decompressing and about 25% in space.
Xcodes now includes the ability to unxip up to 70% faster on some systems.
For simplicity, unxip does not perform any signature verification
